{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"5980db99290a84207e3a709f19726467efeec99187ed73c86f76585d01fc81e6","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:6","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"GDL permit confusables, donor and hearing-impaired options, and commercial license classes","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: GDL permits and restrictions, plus organ donation, hearing-impaired designation and commercial license continuation facts","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: GDL permits and restrictions, plus organ donation, hearing-impaired designation and commercial license continuation facts
Confusable pairs among GDL permits, restrictions and newcomer rules, followed by continuation facts from the organ donation, hearing-impaired and commercial license pages; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A05
Passenger limits differ by permit: a special learner permit allows any parent, guardian or dependent plus one more passenger, while an examination permit allows dependents plus one more unless a parent or guardian rides along. [A05]
Why it matters: group restrictions; confusable special learner versus examination permit passengers.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A05
For examination permit and probationary license holders aged 21 or older, the footnote lifts only the hour, passenger and decal restrictions; it does not mention the phone ban or the seat belt rule. [A05]
Why it matters: group restrictions; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A07
A special learner permit is tied to a student in a training course with an instructor, while an examination permit needs neither student status nor an instructor. [A07]
Why it matters: group permits; confusable special learner versus examination permit.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A06
The special learner permit itself is valid for two years once the instructor buys it. [A06]
Why it matters: group permits; pairs with the two-year test-result rule.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A07
Knowledge test and vision screening results also remain valid for two years. [A07]
Why it matters: group permits; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A02
Option A, the early bird road, is the only road where an approved instructor buys the permit and the MVC validates it only after the behind-the-wheel course. [A02]
Why it matters: group GDL roads; confusable Option A versus Option B.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A04
Option C, the adult road for ages 21 and up, lists only three months of supervised practice on its chart, with no practice-hour minimum. [A04]
Why it matters: group GDL roads; confusable adult versus younger roads.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A06
The work or religion exemption covers only the prohibited driving hours, and the driver must carry the signed letterhead certification while driving then. [A06]
Why it matters: group restrictions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A09
An International Driving Permit adds identification and translation, but a valid driver license must still be carried because the permit cannot replace it. [A09]
Why it matters: group newcomers; confusable IDP versus license.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A09
At age 14 a non-driver ID applicant is asked about the Donate Life Registry, and the question comes again at 18 when applying for an unrestricted license or renewing. [A09]
Why it matters: group registries; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A10
Anyone 14 or older can register as an organ and tissue donor; the family pays nothing, funeral arrangements are not affected, and organs are shared through a national list. [A10]
Why it matters: group registries; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A10
The Next-of-Kin Registry is open to holders of any MVC-issued license, permit or non-driver ID, including a boat license, and contacts can be registered online or by a mailed form. [A10]
Why it matters: group registries; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A11
A hearing-impaired driver license, for a loss of 41 dB or more, is marked with a numerical code and needs verification by a physician or audiologist. [A11]
Why it matters: group designations; difficulty low.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A11
There are three commercial license classes, A, B and C, and none can be applied for without a valid basic Class D New Jersey license or a valid out-of-state CDL. [A11]
Why it matters: group commercial; confusable Class D versus commercial classes.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A11
A Class A license is needed for a tractor trailer or other combination rated at 26,001 pounds or more when the towed vehicle is rated above 10,000 pounds, and it also covers Classes B, C and D with the proper endorsements. [A11]
Why it matters: group commercial; difficulty medium.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A12
A Class B license covers any vehicle rated at 26,001 pounds or more, including one towing a trailer rated at 10,000 pounds or less, and buses that size built for 16 or more passengers counting the driver. [A12]
Why it matters: group commercial; confusable Class A versus Class B.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A12
A Class C license covers lighter vehicles placarded for hazardous material, buses under 26,001 pounds built for 16 or more passengers, and vehicles carrying 8 to 15 passengers for hire. [A12]
Why it matters: group commercial; difficulty medium.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A12
Taxi drivers, funeral procession drivers, rescue and firefighting apparatus operators, farmers hauling within 150 miles of their farms, and personal-use RV drivers do not need a CDL. [A12]
Why it matters: group commercial; difficulty medium.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A13
The passenger endorsement P requires a road test, age 21 and 3 years of driving experience, and a school bus driver needs both the S and the P endorsements. [A13]
Why it matters: group endorsements; confusable P versus S.
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A13
The hazardous materials endorsement H requires a knowledge test, age 21, and training with retesting every two years, while the tanker endorsement N requires a knowledge test. [A13]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty medium.
Source: [A13 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A14
Restriction L on a commercial license means the driver may not operate a vehicle equipped with air brakes, and all CDL tests come from the separate Commercial Driver Manual. [A14]
Why it matters: group commercial; confusable restriction versus endorsement.
Source: [A14 -> pdf-0029]
